abstract: I study redistribution between inactive, unemployed, and employed agents who are heterogeneous in their preferences and their productive skills in the labor market and at home. The government considers that redistribution across skills is desirable, but redistribution across preferences is not: if everyone has the same preferences, equality is optimal, but if everyone has the same skills, laissez-faire is optimal. In turn, this leads to a simple sufficient statistic to assess any reform: any extra dollar of transfer should go to the agent whose consumption is the furthest below what she would have consumed if everyone had average skills. In high-income countries, the gap between the lowest consumption and the average production is empirically much larger in the labor market than among inactives. Hence, introducing an inactivity benefit, or basic income, would neither be welfare-improving nor optimal for that social welfare function, regardless of labor supply elasticities.
abstract_zh: 我研究的是在劳动力市场与家庭中，偏好和生产技能均存在异质性的非活跃、失业及就业个体之间的再分配问题。政府认为，跨技能再分配是可取的，但跨偏好再分配则不然：若所有人偏好相同，则平等为最优；若所有人技能相同，则自由放任为最优。由此，这引出了一个简单的充分统计量来评估任何改革：每一额外转移支付的美元应流向消费水平最低于其若拥有平均技能时所应消费水平的个体。在高收入国家中，最低消费与平均产出之间的差距在劳动力市场中实证上远大于非活跃群体。因此，引入非活跃津贴或基本收入，无论劳动供给弹性如何，既不会改善福利，也不符合该社会福利函数下的最优状态。
title: Basic income versus fairness: redistribution with inactive agents
title_zh: 基本收入与公平：非活跃主体下的再分配
